summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of dilated non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin, prior strokes, type II diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation presenting with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema. The exacerbation was attributed to high dietary salt intake and intermittent noncompliance with diuretic therapy. He was treated with 160 mg of IV furosemide over two days, resulting in clinical improvement with reduced edema and weight loss from 139 kg to 128.7 kg. His heart function remained stable with an ejection fraction of 30%, and no acute ischemia was noted. Chronic issues including bilateral foot ulcers, blepharitis, and obstructive sleep apnea were monitored, with no signs of infection in the wounds. He was discharged home on his prior medications, including torsemide 60 mg twice daily, with instructions for strict low-salt diet, daily weight monitoring, and follow-up for cardiac MRI, podiatry, and ophthalmology.
